gen-gf-bai-jamjuree-fs-literata: Literata is a serif with sturdy hairlines and slightly heavier thick strokes. Bai Jamjuree, with dowel-like stems and crisp wide-mouthed letters, earns its keep when the words are big and brief.
gen-gf-baloo-2-bitter: Expressive Baloo 2 fills the line with open, generous bowls. Bitter, a slab-serif with a very large lowercase and see-through s, keeps paragraphs sturdy and grounded as the eye moves down.
gen-gf-baloo-2-instrument-sans: Expressive Baloo 2 lets its open counters breathe while Instrument Sans keeps a minimal step from capital to lowercase. Round display bounce against wire-like steadiness is the whole appeal.
gen-gf-baloo-2-poppins: Poppins reads with rope-loose curves and no thick-thin flicker, its tall, sturdy lowercase holding a line steady. Baloo 2 headings add expressive, bowl-filled shapes to that smooth line.
gen-gf-baloo-bhai-2-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans has a pipe-cleaner look, with c ends pointing apart. Baloo Bhai 2 does bold, high-reaching rounds best, while Instrument Sans does quiet, steady running text best.
gen-gf-baloo-bhai-2-mulish: Baloo Bhai 2 stretches its wide-mouthed rounds high toward the top line. Mulish, a sans-serif drawn like bent cable with no swelling or thinning, gives it an approachable partner.
gen-gf-baloo-bhai-2-poppins: Big, round and commanding, Baloo Bhai 2 stretches its wide-mouthed lowercase toward the top line. Poppins brings rope-loose curves and a tall, sturdy lowercase with no thick-thin flicker.
gen-gf-baloo-bhai-2-roboto-slab: Bold rounds that reach high up top, then structured slabs underneath. Baloo Bhai 2 supplies the swagger, while Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with open throats, keeps the text zone dense and precise.
gen-gf-baloo-bhaijaan-2-inter: Tall, open curves give Baloo Bhaijaan 2 a distinctive, commanding band of display type. Inter then smooths the reading, its tube-like lines and big counters carrying the eye along page after page.
gen-gf-baloo-bhaijaan-2-poppins: Baloo Bhaijaan 2 is all commanding, open curves in a tall central band. Poppins, a sans-serif with no hairlines either, carries on with the same loose, rounded curves, so the two speak in one voice.
